 The following contains spoilers for Season 1 of VisionQuest , which debuted its finale on November 10, 2026, on Disney+. 
 Since the release of Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness , Marvel Cinematic Universe fans have been waiting for the next chapter in Wanda Maximoff's story. Her heel turn in the film and subsequent smooshing under the weight of Mount Wundagore rubble couldn't possibly be it. VisionQuest finally changed that with its finale, by suggesting the Scarlet Witch is truly dead.

 Parents often lie to their children. They do it to create magic and wonder, like with the myths of Santa Claus and the Tooth Fairy. More often, they do it to spare them pain, suffering, or to give them hope. The last thing Tommy says to his father in this series is almost a question. He never explicitly asks if Vision thinks their survival means Wanda is still alive, but Vision repeats her line from the finale of their eponymous series. He says "it stands to reason" they all might "say 'hello' again." Sure, it leaves the door open for Elizabeth Olsen to return for a more fitting final chapter. But he's simply giving the fans that same hope he gives Tommy.
 Many MCU Fans Feel Wanda Maximoff Did Not Deserve Her Dubious Fate
 Image via Marvel Studios 
 In the comics, Scarlet Witch was sometimes a villain who always found her way back to being a hero. However, in the MCU, it was the end of her story. While WandaVision was a truly moving examination of grief, there is no denying that Wanda Maximoff enthralled an entire town while facing no consequences beyond her own losses.
 In the subsequent movie, she fully went to the dark side, but the Darkhold corrupted her. The disconnect between the show and Multiverse of Madness made her story feel woefully incomplete. For nearly five years, MCU fans have patiently waited for the next phase of Wanda's story. VisionQuest changed these expectations, or at least it tries to.
 When Vision meets Marvel's first forgotten superhero , the Synthetic Man, in his mindspace, he's forced to confront his role in Wanda's downfall. Specifically, his absence. As "White Vision," he flew away from Westview, taking all of Vision's memories and experiences, even from within the Hex, with him. He abandoned her when she needed him most.
 Could he have prevented her corruption by the Darkhold? That he'll never know is his biggest pain point. Vision's identity struggles weren't even about himself, but rather the fact that as the "true Vision," he ultimately failed the woman he loved. His journey to accepting all this was a way to bring fans along with him.
 MCU fans treated Wanda's death in Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness like it was a mistaken pit stop on a larger journey. VisionQuest changed that perspective by forcing viewers to reckon with its reality alongside Vision.
 VisionQuest Finally Earns Wanda's Ultimate Fate
 Image via Marvel Studios 
 The realities of producing a television show and a film, especially during the height of the pandemic, meant that Wanda Maximoff's story suffered from a disconnect. WandaVision 's penultimate episode showed viewers the deaths of her parents hinted at in Age of Ultron .
 She and Pietro wanted to punish the Avengers, specifically Tony Stark. Yet, when she discovered Ultron's original plan went beyond the Avengers , the twins teamed up with the heroes to stop them. Director Hayward lays it out in Episode 4 of WandaVision . He ties Wanda's actions before joining the Avengers to the accident in Lagos in Civil War .
 From this perspective, even Agatha Harkness was "right" about the source of the Westview anomaly. To them, and to the people under her spell, Wanda seemed in control. They didn't understand the complexities of her break with reality, or in this case, the reality she rewrote. She suffered a kind of psychotic break, and she may have even kept the truth of her actions from herself.
 This is why she was so frazzled in the Parenthood -inspired Episode 7. It was the "denial" part of the stages of grief, but underneath it all, she recognized that she was "the villain," as she told Monica during their confrontation on the lawn. Agatha didn't understand it, either. Her deception with the fake Pietro was her way of finding out.
 That's why "Fietro" asked her how she did it. When she told him she didn't know, it was the truth. The ancient witch's meddling only further delayed Wanda's journey towards acceptance and, ultimately, freeing the town. Once Wanda accessed her full power and the Darkhold corrupted it , she surrendered control again.
 Wanda's final chapter was a tragedy. Viewers couldn't understand that until they saw it from Vision's perspective in VisionQuest 's penultimate episode.
 The VisionQuest Finale Ends With Many Callbacks to Create a Closed Narrative Circle
 Image via Marvel Studios 
 From Vision's line about saying "hello again" to his attempt to help Ultron process his grief with the UltraVision simulation, the finale is full of callbacks. The way series creator Terry Matalas and other storytellers deploy them is what makes VisionQuest the perfect ending to the WandaVision trilogy .
 These aren't mere Easter eggs. They are thematic touchstones to the stories that came before. It even extends to Age of Ultron in the next-to-last conversation Vision has with his "Pops." Vision echoes Ultron's line when he says he is "unbearably naïve," and Ultron echoes him by saying, "a thing isn't beautiful because it lasts."
 This simulation wasn't just about stopping Ultron's attempt to destroy the world. Again (cue laugh track). They both used it to process their grief at losing the loves of their lives. Ultron wanted to punish the world because it took Jocasta from him. Vision wanted to punish himself, which is why he was willing to burn himself out to save everyone.
 What makes VisionQuest even more painful for fans is that it delivers the thing Wanda so desperately wanted: it killed her. Her family was made whole. The MCU still hasn't answered how Wanda conjured Billy and Tommy from nothing in the Hex. Agatha All Along revealed that the reborn Billy could magically place his and his brother's souls into the bodies of children who died the moment the Hex fell.

 Wanda lost everyone, twice. She had no one to help her, and it threw her into a darkness she couldn't survive. Fans waiting for her to return may one day get their wish. Never say "never" in the MCU. VisionQuest brought her family back together, and in doing so, it confirmed that she is truly gone. The remaining Maximoff family and the fans have to grieve it and ultimately accept it together.
